newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria FLN members urge rebellion against leaders.
newsitem.headline: Algeria FLN members urge rebellion against leaders.

text.p: Prominent members of Algeria's former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN) on Tuesday urged activists to rebel against the leadership to chart new policy ahead of parliamentary elections next year.

The disgruntled members, including former prime minister Mouloud Hamrouche and former parliament speaker Abdelaziz Belkhadem, said FLN leaders had driven the party to political bankruptcy through the lack of a programme and stifling critics in the party.

In a statement, the maverick members, who term themselves the Group of 20, called on FLN activists to prepare the party congress before general elections promised by President Liamine Zeroual for the first half of 1997.
Such a call effectively means a rebellion against FLN leaders who want a party congress after the planned elections.
"The preparation of the congress of the party renewal must start by the party militants...by submitting all things to criticism," they said in a statement issued in Algiers.

The FLN ruled Algeria in a single party system for nearly three decades until 1988 youth riots ushered in a multiparty democracy a year later. Radical Islamists beat the FLN in Algeria's first free elections in 1990.

A democracy-minded FLN leadership was toppled in 1995 and replaced by leaders seen as close to President Liamine Zeroual. FLN reformers want the party to fight on its own merits to return to power through free elections.
